name: Observation of J/ψ p resonances consistent with pentaquark states in Λb⁰ → J/ψ K⁻ p decays

significance.quote: The significance of each of these resonances is more than 9 standard deviations.
significance.value: more than 9σ for each of the two resonances

summary.plain: LHCb reported two resonances in the J/ψ p mass spectrum of Λb decays that it describes as consistent with pentaquark states, particles made of five quarks. Hadrons with more than the minimal quark content were proposed in 1964, and the paper notes that earlier claimed pentaquark observations had been shown to be spurious.
summary.technical: Amplitude analysis of Λb0→J/ψK−p decays (3 fb−1, 7 and 8 TeV pp collisions): a satisfactory fit of the J/ψ p mass spectrum needs two Breit-Wigner resonances, each with significance of more than 9 standard deviations, with masses 4380±8±29 MeV (width 205±18±86 MeV) and 4449.8±1.7±2.5 MeV (width 39±5±19 MeV). The preferred JP assignments are of opposite parity, with one state of spin 3/2 and the other 5/2. Interpreted as resonant states they must have minimal quark content ccuud.

title: Observation of J/ψp Resonances Consistent with Pentaquark States in Λb0→J/ψK−p Decays
why_it_matters: Hadrons with more than the minimal quark content (qq̄ or qqq) were proposed by Gell-Mann in 1964 and by Zweig; the paper notes that past claimed observations of pentaquark states have been shown to be spurious, although there is at least one viable tetraquark candidate, the Z(4430)+. Resonances decaying strongly into J/ψ p must have a minimal quark content of ccuud.
